title: First light

brief.story: The bench's status light is dead. The LED and its wiring are already on the board. What's missing is the one part that stops the 9 V supply from pushing as much current through it as it can.
brief.goal: Light LED1 at 10–25 mA using one resistor, without burning the LED out.

hints: The resistor goes between the supply's column (column 3, rows f–j) and the LED's long leg (column 12, rows f–j). Current has to pass through it to reach the LED.
The LED keeps about 2.0 V for itself, so the resistor takes the rest: 9 V − 2.0 V = 7 V.
Ohm's law: R = V / I = 7 V / 0.020 A = 350 Ω. The nearest values in the parts bin are 330 Ω and 390 Ω.
debrief: An LED holds its own voltage at about 2 V whatever you do, so it can't limit its own current. The resistor does that job: I = (9 V − 2.0 V) / R. Without it, only the wires would limit the current and the LED would burn out at once. Every indicator LED on every circuit board has a resistor like this next to it.
